metadata.description: Epoch-1 compiler IR wire: the six manager carriers of PROP-054 §7.4/§14.6, frozen from the landed R3 domain types. One whole value of the level being passed crosses per invocation (`##WHOLE-IR-WIRE`); source/document are one addressed document, documents is the explicit document batch, closure/lane/emitted are one complete final artifact (`##IR-LEVELS`, SPEC-DEBT §8.8). The same document is the R3.4 trace snapshot — no second trace-only IR shape exists. TWO metadata sets sit below and must not be confused: `x-conversion-gates` is what the strict domain decoder OWES on every carrier it is handed, including one a plugin transformed and returned; `x-corpus-producer-oracles` is characterization of what THIS corpus's builtin passes emitted. A plugin may legally return a verifier-valid closure whose anchors the builtin `qualify` would have spelled differently or whose order the builtin `close` would not have chosen — the decoder must accept it, and only the corpus tests hold it to the builtin spelling.
x-conversion-gates: ir_schema == 1 at the manager gate before any invoke, and level/cardinality equal the variant they ride (belt: each is a single-value enum, so a mismatch is already reader-red)

every id is non-blank and free of newline/NUL (`ArtifactId`, `ContributionMeta`, `SourceFormatId`, origins, paths, and a `document_subject`'s `declared_path` plus every `document_provider` coordinate component); a `declared_path` is additionally forward-slashed, since `\` is not a separator to a `paths` selector glob; `BackendId` also matches the id charset
the artifact id/target/frame/mode tuple is one `ArtifactContext::new` row, and a `static-lane` generated_path carries the target's extension
a normal/hoisted contribution's origin coordinate equals its target package coordinate; a hoisted target is an unversioned whole document (no version, no anchor, no pin)
every digest is 64 lowercase hex characters; emitted bytes are canonical padded standard base64 — both validated BEFORE any allocation from them
`raw` re-parses to the authority/doc_path/anchor/pinned_r carried beside it, and a fence delimiter is exactly one character

ARENA BOUNDS, checked before indexing: every `doc_node.parent`, `doc_node.children[]` and `doc_tree.anchors` value is < `doc_tree.nodes.len()`; every closure `seed`, `edge.from`/`edge.to`, occurrence `node` and lane `node` is < the node arena length (`lane.source_node_count` for a lane)

FOREST, checked iteratively and before any descent — total, so no input reaches an index: (a) `doc_tree.nodes` is NON-EMPTY, a typed violation rather than the panic `DocTree::root()` would take, since `DocTree::parse` always mints the synthetic root; (b) node 0 IS that root — level 0, kind `heading`, no `parent` member, no incoming child edge; (c) every non-root node has exactly ONE incoming child edge, claims that parent back (`nodes[c].parent == p` for every `c` in `nodes[p].children`), and is reachable from the root; (d) the walk carries a step bound of `nodes.len() + 1` so a `children` cycle is reported, never followed. Bounds alone are not enough — `DocTree::facts_under` pops a `children` stack and a cycle makes it LOOP FOREVER rather than panic, and a detached ring passes every count while no walk can reach it

SPAN BOUNDS, checked before slicing: `span.start <= span.end <= doc_tree.lines.len()` for every node, and `heading_line < lines.len()` for every non-root node of a non-empty document — `DocTree::text` slices `lines[span]` and panics rather than erroring on an out-of-range value
`doc_tree.anchors[a]` names a node whose `id` is `a`, and each `duplicate_anchors` entry is an anchor that repeats

SET PROJECTION: a member projecting a domain `BTreeSet<String>` (`source_resolution_snapshot.explicit_use_keys`, `embed_resolution_snapshot.explicit_use_keys`) carries its canonical sorted, duplicate-free spelling — otherwise wire→domain→wire silently renormalises and the round-trip is lossy

qualification and absorption typestate align; any planned/applied absorption carries no pending source/embed snapshot, one exact identity-bound plan witness per contribution in order, and each applied normal emission order is exactly the non-absorbed occurrence projection
a link result carries one witness per contribution in order, and a lane brackets each normal occurrence as open/node/[forced-newline]/close with one continuous fence history per contribution

PASS/SNAPSHOT: an `embed` edge exists only once `pending_embeds` is consumed and a `source` edge only once `pending_sources` is — each pass mints its edge kind and clears its own snapshot in one run, so the two can never coexist in any carrier a decoder is handed

EMIT IDENTITY: `target` and `backend` are one id and `producer` is `emit:<backend>`; the artifact id is the one this context ROW rides — equal to the backend id for a builtin static lane and for the custom compatibility row, and the reserved `static-fragment` for the BUILTIN compatibility fragment the `static-md` backend renders. A builtin tape is valid UTF-8 in the framing its OWN emitter writes: a static lane carries the context-owned header/preamble prologue and the ordered contribution markers its emission witnesses declare, while a compatibility fragment carries flattened reversible Markdown with neither of those. Opaque bytes ride a custom target under the compatibility frame. Finally, `bytes_digest` is `independent_bytes_digest(bytes)` = SHA-256 of `le64(26) ‖ "vibe-spec/emitted-bytes/v1" ‖ le64(len) ‖ bytes` — the one digest computable from the wire document alone, so a decoder recomputes it rather than trusting it
x-corpus-producer-oracles: CLOSE ORDER: for a value the BUILTIN `close` produced, TWO witnesses, in this order. (1) EDGE — the `kind == use` edge vector is RECONSTRUCTED from the carried directives, not trusted: per normal contribution in contribution order, walk the reached nodes in traversal order, take each node's OWN `tree.directives.directives`, keep `kind == use`, sort by `line` stably as `use_graph::use_addresses` does, resolve each target by PINLESS address identity to the one carried spec node (missing or ambiguous is a fault, never an index), and append `(from, to, requested_target)` unless that exact tuple is already present — `close.rs:146-197`, where a byte-identical repeat is suppressed while a request differing in pin or raw stays its own edge. Compare to the carrier's vector in exact order and exact requested-target fields; `source`/`embed` edges from later passes are outside this comparison. (2) ORDER — replay `topology::order_by` on the adjacency DERIVED in (1), never on the carrier's edges, and compare node-for-node with the pre-absorb order (the applied plan's occurrences, else the live `emission_order`): declaration-order DFS, Gray/Black colouring, postorder, a Gray target admitted only when it and every node on the current loop suffix is a `contract/…` document (`topology.rs:41-49`). Exact, not merely valid — a legal topological permutation the builtin would not have chosen is still a corpus regression, and deriving the adjacency is what stops (2) from proving only that the order agrees with whatever edges the carrier claims. Two consequences no index comparison could express: the admitted A↔B contract cycle orders `[b, a]` while carrying the edge `0 -> 1`, and two roots sharing nodes yield `[0,1,2]` and `[1,0,3]` from their own declaration orders

QUALIFY SPELLING: for a value the BUILTIN `qualify` produced under `qualify-per-node`, every anchor of a node it VISITED — the applied plan's non-absorbed, first-seen occurrences — is `origin_slug(node_qualification_origin(origin, doc_path))` + `--` + the original label, and `renames` is exactly that audit in visit order then document order. Nothing is claimed about a node qualify SKIPPED: an absorbed or already-seen occurrence keeps whatever its author wrote, which may itself look like a slug

OPAQUE TAPE: the emitted golden's `bytes_b64` decodes to `00 ff 0a` — the exact three bytes `OpaqueTestBackend::new` returns (`emit/opaque_test_vehicle.rs`) — under backend `opaque-test`. Characterization of THIS corpus, never a decode rule: any tape whose EMIT IDENTITY coherence holds is a valid carrier

metadata.description: Level source, cardinality document: one document's raw text plus its typed address and frontend format (`SourceIr`).
IR wire schema epoch; 1 in epoch 1. The manager gates a plugin's declared schema before any invoke.
Level document, cardinality document: one document's parsed tree beside its source (`DocumentIr`).
Level document, cardinality artifact: the parse worklist after every per-document pass (`Documents`). Not a sixth level — a real carrier with artifact cardinality.
Deterministic worklist order; the batch may be empty.
Level closure, cardinality artifact: the ordered multi-seed graph for one final artifact (`ClosureIr`), including qualification/absorption/link typestate and the pending source/embed snapshots.
Level lane, cardinality artifact: one complete artifact after linking and before backend serialisation (`LaneIr`).
Level emitted, cardinality artifact: final artifact bytes plus manager-owned immutable provenance (`EmittedIr`). Bytes are canonical standard base64 with padding.
The only level a `source-document` value may carry; any other level spelling is a reader error.
One addressed document per invocation.
One complete final artifact per invocation.
The compatibility/static-lane policy (`StaticCompileMode`).

Final-artifact target identity (`ArtifactTarget`). Open: a custom backend names itself; the two built-in STATIC targets are fixed. `ArtifactContext::new` admits a custom target only as `(custom, compatibility-fragment, _, artifact == backend id)`, and it is the only target whose emitted tape is opaque — `emit.rs::prepare_target` maps a builtin to a Markdown/XML tape the emit pass re-reads. Strict R6.2b conversion owns and preserves every valid backend id so every valid corpus carrier round-trips without an undocumented refusal; R6.3 separately owns registration, implementation selection and invocation. Identity does not imply that an implementation is installed.
The authority half of a `spec://` address (`Authority`).
An undotted authority; parses but never resolves.
Raw `@`-spec, unparsed; absent for an unversioned address.
A fully qualified `spec://` address (`SpecAddress`), carried field-by-field; conversion re-checks the fields against `raw`.
The address exactly as written, including any `~rN`.
Document path under the `spec/` root, `/`-joined, genre included.
Tree path segments; empty means the whole document.
Spec-unit revision pin (`~rN`); absent when unpinned.
A document's compiler identity (`DocumentAddress`): a real `spec://` address, or a simple static entry's provider/path identity.
An ungrouped host's simple static entry — no honest spec address exists for it.
Half-open source-line range `[start, end)`.
metadata.x-conversion: `start <= end <= doc_tree.lines.len()` — validated BEFORE slicing; `DocTree::text` indexes `lines[span]` and panics on an out-of-range value.

metadata.description: One node of the document arena (`doctree::Node`): a heading section or a `##<ID>` fact leaf.
metadata.x-conversion: `heading_line < lines.len()` for every non-root node of a non-empty document; `parent` and every `children` entry are < `nodes.len()`, and together they form a FOREST rooted at index 0 (each child claims its parent back, one incoming edge per non-root, no cycle) — validated BEFORE indexing the arena, because a `children` cycle makes `DocTree::facts_under` loop rather than panic. A node carries an `id` only when its source line declares that anchor (`{#id}` on a heading, `##<ID>`/`@fact:<ID>` as a fact's lead token); a heading id the line does not carry is unreachable through `DocTree::parse`.

metadata.description: Heading level 1..=6; 0 for the synthetic root and for fact leaves.
Heading text with `#`s and `{#anchor}` stripped; empty for a fact leaf.
Text after the `{#anchor}` on the heading line (merge markers); empty when absent.
0-based source line of the heading, or the first line of a fact leaf's span.
Source lines this node covers, subtree included.
Arena indices of child nodes in document order.
The `{#anchor}` or `##<ID>` label; absent when none was declared.
Arena index of the parent node; absent only for the root.
A parsed `#embed` / `#use` / `#source` directive (`Directive`).
Raw options between the keyword and the address; may be empty.
0-based source line.
An `@spec://…` in-place use (`InPlaceUse`) — mandatory to read on first encounter.
A malformed directive or `@spec`, reported rather than fatal (`DirectiveError`).
metadata.x-conversion: Scanner diagnostics only — the five shapes `Directives::parse` emits (missing address, bad address, bad `@spec`, duplicate alias, undeclared `@!`). A duplicate fact id is NOT one of them: it lands in `doc_tree.duplicate_anchors`.

metadata.description: Everything a directive scan finds, in document order (`Directives`), kept beside the tree so close never rescans raw text.
`#use … as <Alias>` bindings; first declaration wins, duplicates are reported in `errors`.
The complete document IR (`DocTree`): node arena, anchor index, duplicate-anchor record, source lines and the directive scan.
The arena; index 0 is the synthetic root.
Flat anchor → arena index; a repeated anchor keeps its first occurrence here.
Each extra occurrence of a repeated anchor; empty means every anchor is unique — the `DuplicateId` verdict input.
The document's source lines; spans index into this vector.

The typed provider identity a document subject carries (`DocumentProvider`, PROP-054 `##CONTRIB-SELECTOR`): the value a source/document selector's `packages` dimension is matched against, spelled as typed coordinate components rather than a rendered display string. The carrier is TOTAL — every document names one arm, and there is no missing-key spelling of absence. The four coordinate arms mirror the kernel's dependency-coordinate and host shapes exactly (`DependencyProviderId`; `HostIdentity`'s ungrouped / coordinate / virtual-workspace spellings), so a match-time adapter reconstructs the typed identity without parsing anything. The two remaining arms are the two DIFFERENT absences, and a full-IR plugin must be able to tell them apart: `unclaimed` says no owner exists to name, `undetermined` says an owner exists and was not resolved. Collapsing them would hand a selector adapter one input for two verdicts.

No contribution row declared this document into this artifact, so no provider is claimed. A PERMANENT and correct answer: the address' authority names the package that owns the document, which is not the question a `packages` dimension asks. An authored `packages` dimension matching nothing is the final verdict here, not a placeholder. Every document the compiler REACHED through `#use`, `#source` or `#embed` carries this arm.

A contribution row DID declare this document, and the producer could not determine which typed provider that row names. A TEMPORARY answer, and the one every document written by today's producers carries: they receive the declaring owner as a display string, and the typed identity reaches the subject only through the owner-view adapter. A selector adapter may not read it as `unclaimed`'s matches-nothing — the honest reading is that the answer is not yet known.
An installed dependency provider's versionless coordinate.
A host project with no group, named exactly as authored.
A grouped project or package-role host, carrying the same validated coordinate a dependency does.
A coordinator that may control dependencies but declares none; it has no coordinate components.

The immutable selector subject of ONE addressed document (`DocumentSubject`): the provider a source/document selector's `packages` dimension matches and the path its `paths` dimension matches. Per addressed document, never per artifact. It is CARRIED, not re-derived — a contribution's `declared_path` is the path the contributing row declared and may legitimately differ from its address' `doc_path` — and the inter-pass verifier refuses a source/document transform that rewrites either member. Required: a decoder refuses a carrier that omits it rather than inventing one, because an invented subject would silently change which transforms a document is in scope for.

The document's declared path, forward-slashed and case-sensitive (the selector adapter contract). Conversion rejects a blank or newline-bearing value, and also a backslashed one: the kernel compiles a `paths` glob with a literal separator, so `\` is not a separator to any pattern and a backslashed path silently matches nothing. The refusal is a refusal, never a normalisation — rewriting the separator would invent an identity the producer did not state.
Source IR payload (`SourceIr`): typed address, frontend format, immutable document subject, raw text.

Open frontend identity (`SourceFormatId`), e.g. `markdown`, `xml`, or a registered custom format. Deliberately not a closed vocabulary: frontends register without a schema bump. Conversion rejects a blank value.
Parsed document IR (`DocumentIr`): the tree with its source beside it, so exact text/newline identity survives while the tree is span-indexed.
Markdown fence state at one occurrence boundary (`LinkFenceSnapshot`).
No fence is open.
The fence character (`` ` `` or `~`); conversion validates exactly one char.
Delimiter run length.
One origin-qualification rename (`RenameEntry`).
One rename together with the origin whose namespace produced it (`OriginRename`).
Provenance of one top-level contribution in effective-boot order (`ContributionMeta`); conversion rejects blank values.
One exact request for a shared logical closure node (`ClosureOccurrence`).
Index into `closure.nodes`.
READ-ONCE disposition aligned to one contribution occurrence (`AbsorptionOccurrence`); identity is the exact spec address, never a bool mask.
One closed document payload (`ClosureDocument`): a graph node while addressed by an id, a simple contribution's lowered payload outside the graph.
This document's declared `#use … as` bindings.
One ordered edge of the closure graph (`ClosureEdge`).
Index into `closure.nodes`.
The three authored dependency relations (`ClosureEdgeKind`).
One top-level contribution after the batch closes into a graph (`ClosureContribution`).
Root node index into `closure.nodes`.
Exact emission sequence; a node id may repeat or be shared by several roots.
A simple contribution's whole lowered document, carried outside the graph.
A whole-document hoist; the target is an unversioned whole document.
Runtime typestate of the qualify transform (`QualificationState`).
The analyzed occurrence sequence bound to its exact contribution identity (`ContributionAbsorption`).
The immutable pre-qualification overlap judgment for one artifact (`AbsorptionPlan`).
Runtime typestate of READ-ONCE absorption (`AbsorptionState`): the identity-bound plan crosses both boundaries; no side table holds it.
Exact top-level identity consumed by link, including empty contributions (`LinkContributionWitness`).
One resolved occurrence (`LinkOccurrence`): semantics only, never backend marker bytes.
Index of the owning contribution.
Occurrence index within the contribution.
Typed reversible-marker key (`LinkMarkerKey`).
Canonical result of linking one whole artifact (`LinkResult`).
SHA-256 of the semantic input, 64 lowercase hex chars; validated at conversion.
Runtime typestate of the link transform (`LinkState`).
One observed source document (`DocumentObservation`).
One observed `#embed` expansion (`ExpansionObservation`).
Artifact-wide immutable observation of every source input (`SourceResolutionSnapshot`).
Keys of `documents` in discovery order.
Keyed by the address without its pin.
Keyed by the full address string.

metadata.x-conversion: Projects a domain `BTreeSet<String>`: only the canonical sorted, duplicate-free spelling survives wire→domain→wire unchanged (see SET PROJECTION).

metadata.description: Artifact-wide immutable observation of every embed input (`EmbedResolutionSnapshot`).

metadata.x-conversion: Projects a domain `BTreeSet<String>`: only the canonical sorted, duplicate-free spelling survives wire→domain→wire unchanged (see SET PROJECTION).

metadata.description: Frame policy surrounding all contributions of one artifact (`ArtifactFrame`).
Path of the generated artifact; conversion rejects blank and newline-bearing values.
The one-seed `compile_static*` compatibility fragment frame.
Immutable identity and policy copied through every artifact-level IR (`ArtifactContext`); conversion re-validates the id/target/frame/mode tuple.
Open artifact identity (`ArtifactId`), e.g. `static-xml`.
The ordered multi-seed graph for one final artifact (`ClosureIr`). Nothing lives in a manager-side table: typestate and snapshots ride the value.
The closure arena; edge/contribution ids index it.
Effective-boot order.
Document order per origin.
Present until the source fold has consumed it.
Present until the embed expansion has consumed it.
Semantic frame data shared by every concrete lane backend (`LaneFrame`).
Absent for the compatibility fragment.
One exact linked occurrence (`LaneNode`); marker policy is closed by type.
Index into the source closure's node arena.
Backend-neutral framing and body chunks for one contribution (`LaneChunk`); concrete comment or newline bytes stay the emit backend's responsibility.
One top-level contribution in exact effective-boot order, assembled (`LaneContribution`).
One complete artifact after linking and before backend serialisation (`LaneIr`).
SHA-256 of the link input, 64 lowercase hex chars; validated at conversion.
One contribution's emission witness (`EmissionContributionWitness`).
SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex chars; validated at conversion.
SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex chars; validated at conversion.
Immutable evidence created by the manager at the backend boundary (`EmissionProvenance`).
Backend identity (`BackendId`), e.g. `static-xml`; conversion validates the id charset.
Stable name of the emit pass that produced the bytes (`PassName`), e.g. `emit:static-xml`.
SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex chars; validated at conversion.

Schedule pass names of the emitted-position transforms that rewrote these bytes, in application order (`transform:emitted:<key>`, a `PassName`); empty means no emitted transform changed the artifact. Conversion validates every element through the same non-blank scalar law `producer` obeys.
SHA-256 of the emitted bytes, 64 lowercase hex chars; validated at conversion. Recomputed after an emitted transform, so it is always the digest of the bytes actually carried.
Final artifact bytes plus manager-owned immutable provenance (`EmittedArtifact`).
Canonical standard base64 with padding (`A-Za-z0-9+/`, `=` padding), no whitespace; opaque bytes, never assumed UTF-8. Validated at conversion and by the corpus reader.
